item.title: Region Coloring of Spatial Graphs using Knot-theoretic Ternary Quasigroups
item.description: arXiv:2611.17379v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct coloring conditions around vertices for region colorings of unoriented spatial graph diagrams by knot-theoretic ternary quasigroups. These conditions require cyclic products of left and right operators around each vertex to be the identity. We prove that the resulting coloring sets are preserved under the generalized Reidemeister moves and relate our construction to the palette framework. We show that the vertex coloring conditions are automatic for Dehn tribrackets and determine the associated palettes for unoriented Alexander tribrackets. We also introduce an additional restriction on vertex colorings that is preserved under the fifth Reidemeister move for every unoriented knot-theoretic ternary quasigroup. This restriction gives rise to further coloring invariants for Dehn tribrackets and unoriented Alexander tribrackets.
item.dc:creator: Mitsuru Kuramoto

item.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
item.description: arXiv:2611.17557v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$. If $C_f\to G$ denotes the free crossed module determined by $f$, then the associated crossed modules of $R_f$ and $Q_f$ are both isomorphic to $C_f\to G$. We also characterize free augmented quandles in terms of stabilizers. As applications, we prove that the canonical inner augmentation of every generalized Alexander quandle is free and that the canonical inner augmentation of a classical knot quandle is free if and only if the knot is a torus knot, whereas for every $n$-knot with $n\geq2$ it is free.
item.dc:creator: Toshiyuki Akita, Sota Takase

item.title: The Gaps Between the $\Delta$-Unknotting Number and Its Lower Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2611.17624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $u^{\Delta}(K)$ denote the $\Delta$-unknotting number of a knot $K$, and let $a_2(K)$ denote the second coefficient of the Conway polynomial. It is known that $u^{\Delta}(K)\geq |a_2(K)|$. We define the $\Delta$-gap of $K$ by $G^{\Delta}(K):=u^{\Delta}(K)-|a_2(K)|$. In this paper, we investigate the behavior of this invariant for various families of knots. For example, we prove that the $\Delta$-gap of the pretzel knot $K=P(2s, 4s-1,4s+1)$, where $s$ is a positive integer, satisfies $G^{\Delta}(K) \geq 4s$. Consequently, the $\Delta$-gap is unbounded. To further investigate the structure of the $\Delta$-gap, we distinguish between $\Delta$-moves that increase $a_2(K)$ and those that decrease it, since each $\Delta$-move changes $a_2(K)$ by $\pm1$. We analyze how these two types of moves contribute to the $\Delta$-gap. We also investigate the gaps between $u^{\Delta}(K)$ and other knot invariants that provide lower bounds for it. In particular, we establish explicit formulas and lower bounds for these gaps for certain families of pretzel knots, torus knots, two-bridge knots, and Montesinos knots. Our results show that these gaps can be arbitrarily large. In addition, we identify prime positive knots with $u^{\Delta}(K)=2$ or $3$, and propose a conjecture on a lower bound for $u^{\Delta}(K)$ for prime positive knots.
item.dc:creator: Kazumichi Nakamura

item.title: An Obstruction to Realizing Aspherical $3$-Manifold Groups via Torus Surgery
item.description: arXiv:2611.18461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Y$ be a closed, connected, oriented, aspherical $3$-manifold with fundamental group $\pi = \pi_1(Y)$ and positive first Betti number $\beta_1(Y) > 0$, and let $X_0 = Y \times S^1$. We prove that no torus surgery on $X_0$ along a torus-fibered $T^2$-knot $T \subseteq X_0$ can yield a $4$-manifold $X = X_{0; T, f}$ with fundamental group $\pi$. The obstruction combines the vanishing of the Euler characteristic of $X$ with a classifying-map argument showing that the unimodular intersection form on $H^2(X; \mathbb{Z})$ must admit an isotropic subgroup of rank $\beta_1(\pi)$, forcing $\chi(X) \geq 2$. Along the way, we also present an independent geometric proof via covering space theory, the Sphere Theorem, and Scott's Core Theorem that the fundamental group of a closed aspherical $3$-manifold is torsion-free.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Meyer

item.title: Vector bundles on spin K\"ahler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.17647v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin K\"ahler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an existence theorem for singular Fueter sections and multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten solutions that holds for every Riemannian metric on a large class of 4-manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Minh Lam Nguyen, Ollie Thakar

item.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
item.description: arXiv:2611.18237v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Nicosanti, Pavel Putrov, Johann Quenta-Raygada

item.title: Quandle Cohomology Quiver Representations
item.description: arXiv:2411.02153v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define a family of quiver representation-valued invariants of oriented classical and virtual knots and links associated to a choice of finite quandle $X$, abelian group $A$, set of quandle 2-cocycles $C\subset H^2_Q(x;A)$, choice of coefficient ring $k$ and set of quandle endomorphisms $S\subset \mathrm{Hom}(X,X)$. From this representation we define four new polynomial (or ``polynomial'' depending on $A$) invariants. We generalize to the case of biquandles and compute some examples.
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson

item.title: Triangulations of the 3-sphere with knotted edge
item.description: arXiv:2411.18938v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for any knot $K$, there exists a one-vertex triangulation of the $3$-sphere containing an edge forming $K$. The proof is constructive, and based on fully augmented links. We use our method to produce ``complicated'' simplicial triangulations of the $3$-sphere that we show are smallest possible, up to a constant multiplicative factor.
item.dc:creator: Dionne Ibarra, Daniel V. Mathews, Jessica S. Purcell, Jonathan Spreer

item.title: Geometry for Kleinian Groups Generated by a Parabolic Pair
item.description: arXiv:2512.17044v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper develops a computational framework for studying the hyperbolic geometry of 2-bridge link complements and Kleinian groups generated by two parabolic elements. The framework is built on Sakuma-Weeks triangulations and introduces a family of Farey recursive polynomials. For a rational number which determines a hyperbolic 2-bridge link, this paper provides a simple recursive algorithm to determine a Farey recursive polynomial which has a root which determines the geometry of the link complement. This root is the shape parameter for a pair of tetrahedra in the Sakuma-Weeks triangulation. Using the same polynomials, the paper defines rational functions, one function for each edge in the Farey graph. Evaluating these rational functions at the root yields the complete collection of shape parameters for the triangulation. The Riley slice and its exterior lie in the complex plane and are traditionally viewed as parameter spaces for two-parabolic generated subgroups of PSL(2,C). This paper's triangulation-based approach provides a more geometric perspective to these parameter spaces. The Farey recursive methods apply throughout the Riley slice and its exterior, enabling computations for quotient orbifolds of Kleinian groups generated by parabolic pairs, incomplete hyperbolic spaces with non-discrete parameter groups, and others. Explicit calculations include the cusp groups in the boundary of the Riley slice and singly augmented 2-bridge link complements. Applications include: explicit computation of fundamental domains and holonomies for 2-bridge link complements; a precise correspondence between group elements and crossing circles in tangle diagrams; determination of cusp fields for 2-bridge links; geometric analysis of algebraic and geometric limits arising from Dehn surgery on singly augmented 2-bridge links; and explicit triangulations of Heckoid orbifolds.
item.dc:creator: Eric Chesebro

item.title: A Faithful Action of the Mapping Class Group $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ on the $(2g-1)$-Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.10577v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that $\mathrm{Mod}(S_g)$ acts faithfully by orientation-preserving homeomorphisms on a $(2g-1)$-sphere when $g \geq 3$ using equivariant blow-up and bi-orderability of the Torelli group.
item.dc:creator: Shile Wang

item.title: Bestvina metric and tree reduction for $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2602.17982v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We reduce the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture for all Artin groups to properties of Artin groups whose Coxeter diagrams are trees, from which we deduce new classes of Artin groups satisfying the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture. This relies on constructing actions of Artin groups on Bestvina complexes of suitable Garside groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Jingyin Huang

item.title: From Trees to Tripods: Proof of $K(\pi,1)$ for Artin groups with $ABI$-type spherical parabolics
item.description: arXiv:2602.17983v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe contractibility criteria for typed simplicial complexes modeled on Coxeter diagrams. Such complexes include buildings and also arise as coset complexes of groups with strongly admissible parabolic systems, including Shephard groups, which generalize both Artin and Coxeter groups. Our result applies to a large class of complexes modeled on \emph{tree Coxeter diagrams} and implies deformation retraction onto a nonpositively curved subcomplex. As an application, we reduce the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture for all Artin groups with tree Coxeter diagrams to properties of Artin groups with tripod-shaped Coxeter diagrams. Combining this reduction theorem and properties of braid groups in previous works of Charney, Crisp-McCammond, Haettel and the second named author, we deduce that the $K(\pi,1)$-conjecture holds for every Artin group whose spherical parabolic subgroups avoid type $D_n$ ($n \ge 4$) and the exceptional types. We give an analogous tree to tripod reduction for Shephard groups. Our proof relies on two ingredients of independent interest: a notion of combinatorial convexity and a Bestvina-type inequality in certain injective orthoscheme complexes. These ingredients further rely on the use of structural properties of bi-Helly graphs developed in joint work of the first named author with Munro.of bi-Helly graphs (also known as absolute bipartite retracts) developed in joint work of the first named author with Munro.
item.dc:creator: Nima Hoda, Jingyin Huang

item.title: Ahlfors--Weill Extension, Asymptotically Conformal Curves and Epstein--Poincar\'{e} Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.02171v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Ahlfors--Weill construction explicitly extends a univalent function $f$ with Schwarzian norm less than $1/2$ to a quasiconformal homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere, an extension that can be understood geometrically through Epstein surfaces. For asymptotically conformal curves, the uniformization map can be extended to a larger disk, and Loewner theory can be used to verify that this extension is quasiconformal. In this paper, we construct a local quasireflection with such an extension. Using this local quasireflection, we modify classical estimates of Ahlfors and show that domains bounded by asymptotically conformal curves have asymptotically similar hyperbolic and quasihyperbolic metrics. Furthermore, by combining these estimates with a geometric reinterpretation of the extension through Epstein surfaces, we show that the Epstein-Poincar\'e surfaces of the complementary domains are arbitrarily close to one another near the curve.
item.dc:creator: Ming Hong Tee
